title: AI office (multi-agent workspace on Claude Code)
tagline: A template for a multi-agent workspace built on Claude Code: one main agent routes work to specialist agents, and a live page shows what each one is doing.
problem: Once more than one AI agent works for you, it gets hard to tell which one has a task, what it finished and what is waiting on an answer, and each new session starts without the facts the last one learned.
built: Built on Claude Code, and it runs inside Claude Code. A handbook makes the session opened in the folder the main agent, which routes each request to a specialist "desk": a subagent with its own mission, home folder and limits. Desks share a memory of small notes, report on a status board and write a work log. A live page draws the office as an animated floor where I read reports, send instructions and answer a desk's question with a button. The repository is a template of my own office, with three example desks and example memory and status files.
highlights: A hook stops a desk from finishing until its status file and the work log have changed; it blocks once and says what is missing
By the handbook's rules a push, merge, deletion or sent message is never run from the live page alone: the main agent asks in chat first
An instruction sent while no session is open waits in the inbox, and the next session picks it up
The README lists its limits: the model follows the approval rules and no code enforces them; the hook checks that files changed, not that they are true
testing: There is no automated test suite, and the README says so. The hook was checked by hand with simulated start and stop events; the page script was checked for syntax and run once with a stubbed browser and sample desks. The template has not been published as a fresh live page, so that path was not re-tested.
